Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

This role sits within User Policy Operations. User Policy Operations assesses the risk that users pose to Stripe against our Terms of Service and related policies. Its work helps ensure that the businesses we support are aligned with those policies, and it protects Stripe, our partners, and the broader user community. We strive to deliver frictionless experiences for all of our users, whether they are an Independent Business, Startup, SMB, or Enterprise, and our mission is to provide every Stripe user with the best support experience possible.

What you’ll do

In this role, you will be a player-coach leading a team of Risk Operations associates who assess complex and unique user situations against Stripe's Terms of Service and related policies. Their assessments determine whether Stripe can continue to support these users. Many of them are among Stripe's most strategic, so the work calls for urgency, sound judgment, and a clear view of the risk each user poses to Stripe.

Your team will often work beyond the written workflow and policy. They will dig into the facts of each case, assess the risk to Stripe, and turn that into clear, well-reasoned recommendations. As their leader, you will help them move quickly through ambiguity, get up to speed fast on the situations they're handling, and work through friction when engaging across the risk ecosystem, including cross-functional partners and account teams. Through clear goals, guidance, and mentorship, you will set both individuals and the team up for success.

To be a fit, you will have a coaching mindset, proven ability to communicate at different levels, a track record of driving operational performance, and a passion for inspiring a team to deliver outstanding results.In this role, you will act in a player-coach capacity and are accountable for supporting Risk/Partner Risk Operations associates.  

Responsibilities

  • Lead and coach a team of associates conducting Terms of Service evaluations and risk assessments on complex and strategic users, determining whether those users remain aligned with Stripe's policies and whether Stripe can continue to support them
  • Coach your team to think beyond what is written in policy: to investigate thoroughly, weigh the broader risk a user presents to Stripe, and make sound, well-documented recommendations in ambiguous or unprecedented situations
  • Manage your team through complex risk situations, including those that require cross-functional engagement and close collaboration with account teams and other partners across the risk ecosystem
  • Quickly understand the cases your team is working on, and help remove blockers and navigate friction points when working across teams
  • Foster a sense of urgency on strategic user cases, balancing speed with quality, rigor, and consistency of decisions
  • Support and coach your team in conducting thorough investigations of merchant accounts to facilitate progressive and sustainable business growth
  • Ongoing management of the operational performance of your team to deliver KPIs and report to key stakeholders
  • Help scale our operations and improve user experience by identifying process and policy improvements, including gaps surfaced through complex case work
  • Manage capacity and scheduling, dividing and assigning work between team members, including routing complex and time-sensitive cases appropriately
  • Ensure your team has all the skills and resources needed to be successful in their role
  • Set clear goals and expectations for individual and team performance
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement to refine team processes and procedures
  • Support recruitment and hiring initiatives
  • Contribute to 20% core work on a daily basis
  • Coach and mentor individuals to meet career goals via structured development conversations
  • Provide continuous performance feedback and facilitate periodic formal performance reviews
  • Drive and own initiatives that make the team a warm and welcoming place to work
  • Keep the team engaged and motivated towards their work

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • A minimum of 6+ years of experience in risk operations or policy/supportability operations
  • Experience coaching/leading operations teams and managing performance
  • Experience mentoring others and are able to constructively provide feedback to others
  • Experience in delivering weekly and monthly business metrics and reporting
  • Proven ability to be a subject matter expert in Risk Operations
  • Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment in ambiguous situations, assessing risk beyond written policy and making clear, defensible recommendations
  • Ability to work cross functionally, including with account teams and stakeholders supporting strategic users, to deliver best results and promote partnership
  • Ability to work with urgency and manage competing priorities in a fast-moving environment
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in both English and Spanish
  • Exemplary planning and time management skills

Preferred qualifications

  • Knowledge of risk reviews, knowledge in policy/compliance operations, and fraud detection tools
  • Experience managing risk events in the system, and identify the at-risk scenario.

About the position

We're opening our first internships in the Formal Methods group of our OCaml Language team, which develops language features and tooling for correctness reasoning and bug finding in OCaml programs. With the emergence of agentic programming, we think formal methods will play a major role in helping validate agent-generated code and providing feedback for agents. Our vision is to make formal methods as useful a tool for building software as type systems are for us today, both by leveraging existing tools and technology, and pursuing novel approaches. 

During the internship, we want to give you a real sense of what it's like to work at Jane Street full time while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. You'll be paired with full-time employees who act as mentors, collaborating with you on a real-world project that combines your research background with one of our active projects, such as adding support for property-based testing of formal specifications or developing a refinement type system for functional correctness verification. You’ll have the opportunity to evaluate the tools you develop on a large, actively developed production codebase. You'll also be able to attend guest speakers and social events, and hopefully get a real sense of what it would be like to work here full-time.

There is plenty of work on combining agents and formal methods. What’s different at Jane Street is that we aren't stuck designing verification tools for legacy languages: we can modify and improve OxCaml, our branch of OCaml, and its development environment to make them well-suited for proof-driven software development. Moreover, we have a community of excellent programmers who are eager to adopt these tools and apply them to real software.

Learn more about Jane Street's internship program here.

About you

We're looking for PhD students, postdocs, and masters students with outstanding research experience in program verification, programming language semantics, property-based testing, static analysis, model checking, and related areas. You should be

  • A strong programmer who enjoys collaborating in small teams
  • Excited to turn research ideas into practical tools
  • Intellectually curious, humble and unafraid to ask questions 

We don't expect you to have a background in finance, OCaml, or functional programming.

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

Principal Engineer, Data Quality Platform

You'll own data correctness across Talos. You'll lead the data quality engineering team, run BAU data operations, and own reference and security master data, along with the pipelines and platform that deliver it.

Our goal: the data we return to clients is always correct, and we find defects before a client does.

You'll join a small team with the mandate to work independently from product engineering and challenge it. Engineering teams make assumptions about how their systems behave. Your job is to test those assumptions and prove or disprove them with evidence.

 

Responsibilities

Lead AI-first data quality engineering

  • Validate every client-facing endpoint continuously. The focus is our REST and WebSocket APIs. Cloud delivery (S3, Snowflake, Databricks) is also in scope. Assert correctness against independent sources of truth, across every environment and client entitlement.

  • Cover streaming as well as request/response. For WebSocket, that means:

    • Sequencing and gap detection

    • Snapshot-to-increment consistency

    • Reconnect and replay correctness

    • Staleness of live subscriptions

    • Agreement between the streamed view and the REST view of the same state

  • Use adaptive detection, not static thresholds. Learn baselines per endpoint and per market, and let them adjust as "normal" changes. Hand-set limits get noisy, go stale, and teach people to ignore alerts.

  • Apply LLM and agentic tooling to generate checks from API specs and schemas, keep them current as the product changes, and triage alerts before a human sees them. Know when a deterministic rule, invariant or cross-source reconciliation is the better tool.

  • Test resilience and load. Design load, performance and failure-mode tests.

  • When you find a fault, raise it with the owning team with enough evidence for them to act. Drive it to resolution, then add a check that would have caught it earlier.

  • Measure and publish endpoint and field coverage, time to detect, detected-before-client rate and false-positive rate.

Run data governance

  • Build and maintain a catalog of our data assets and APIs, covering lineage and downstream consumers. Maintain an understanding of assets, how they're used and what breaks when they change.

  • Own data governance tooling such as OpenMetadata.

Own reference and security master data

  • Lead the build-out of the next-generation security master platform, then run it day to day: new listings, symbol mapping across venues, and increment and contract specs.

  • Design processes for safe updates to security entries, with validation and rollback.

Expand coverage across the firm

  • Over time, extend data quality coverage beyond client APIs to:

    • Trade signals

    • Pre-trade analytics

    • Client post-trade analysis

    • PMS analytics

Qualifications

  • A track record of leading data QA or data quality teams, preferably on market data or other high-throughput, real-time data.

  • A deep understanding of streaming and API behaviour: throughput, WebSocket semantics, ordering, recovery and failure modes.

  • Experience inventorying and testing a large API and data surface end to end.

  • Hands-on experience with data governance: cataloging, lineage, ownership.

  • Experience with performance and load testing of distributed systems.

  • A strong engineering background. You design platforms, not scripts on a cron job, and you build on shared infrastructure rather than creating one-off tooling.

  • Practical experience applying LLM and agentic tooling to engineering problems.

Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Marketing Operations team is responsible for the systems, processes, and data infrastructure that power Stripe's global marketing engine. We partner closely with Growth Product, Growth Marketing, Regional Demand and Field Marketing, Lifecycle Marketing, Sales Development, and Marketing Technology teams to ensure campaigns are executed with precision with as much automation as possible, prospect and performance data are accurate and actionable, and our marketing technology stack operates at scale.

We are systems thinkers and operational leaders focused on improving the workflows, tooling, data quality, and processes that enable marketing and sales teams to move faster and more effectively. Our work spans campaign operations, marketing automation, prospect data management, lead management, pre-and post event operations, cross-functional program delivery, and more.

We are looking for a Marketing Technology Program Manager. This role sits at the intersection of technology, data, and program management, and it requires someone who can move fluidly between strategic planning and hands-on execution.

Drive technology programs that power Stripe's marketing engine. Lead cross-functional programs with product, engineering, and marketing stakeholders. Drive improvements and innovation through AI, process automation, and 1st and 3rd party tools. Deliver the systems that enable marketing teams to move faster, continuously improve performance, and remove bottlenecks.

Responsibilities

  • Act as the program manager for 1-2 initiatives at a time. Examples include the following.
    • Digital channel effectiveness: Improve digital campaign performance through personalization, content optimization, audience optimization. Include recommendation system interlock.
    • Measurement: Give every campaign a consistent identity; connect marketing activity, spend, engagement, leads, and downstream outcomes.
    • Account-Based Marketing (ABM): Identify target accounts, coordinate account-based campaigns, personalize account experiences, capture engagement, measure account penetration.
    • Online Event Production & Community: Digital event promotion, registration, online attendance, content delivery, community engagement, and follow-up/measurement.
  • Program management responsibilities include
    • Own end-to-end program delivery for initiatives; maintain program communications, track milestones, lead cross-functional workstreams, and provide regular updates on roadmap progress
    • Lead programs to address recurring marketing process and technology challenges; define objectives, success metrics, and build repeatable processes that scale
    • Partner with product and engineering teams to scope business requirements, coordinate discovery, and translate operational needs into product requirements for internal tooling
    • Lead requirements, selection, contracting, implementation, and adoption of third party software; drive new custom features in the company’s implementation of third party software
    • Coordinate review cycles, pilots, and feedback collection during program execution; summarize required changes, identify launch-blocking issues, and escalate risks as needed
    • Drive ongoing operations improvements through process innovation, automation, and the adoption of AI-powered tools to increase productivity and transform workflows
    • Maintain scalable documentation and support coordination with offshore production teams and cross-functional partners across time zones

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 6+ years of experience in B2B marketing operations/technology or a related program management role in a high-growth technology environment
  • 3+ years of experience working day-to-day on some or all of the following: marketing automation platforms, CRM platforms, audience targeting and personalization, marketing campaign measurement, account based marketing, and online events (webinars)
  • 3+ years of experience in end-to-end program management of cross-functional marketing, sales, and engineering initiatives
  • Experience building AI agents, including examples of agents you have deployed and examples of ways you are using AI on a daily basis beyond chat
  • 3+ years of experience doing your own analysis using queries, dashboards, and AI and partnering with analysts and data scientists for more complex analytics needs
  • 3+ years of experience defining your own scope and goals and collaborating with a distributed, global team to deliver on them
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to convey complex operational concepts to diverse stakeholders across marketing, sales, and engineering

Preferred qualifications

    • Experience managing prospect or marketing database programs, including data enrichment, hygiene, and growth using first-party and third-party data sources
    • 3+ years of experience with marketing technology systems and platforms, including Marketo, customer data platforms, marketing channel and campaign measurement and attribution, account based marketing platforms, and online event platforms
    • Experience selecting and managing third-party software in a B2B marketing context
    • Experience implementing AI tools to improve marketing operations workflows and productivity
    • Experience working with global teams on a day-to-day basis
    • Knowledge of data privacy and compliance frameworks
    • Experience in the financial services, payments, or B2B software industries
